coaching.summary: The decision captures the core revenue mechanics well, but the model currently treats Monthly Recurring Revenue as the sole success measure and does not account for how a price change ripples into customer lifetime value or competitive positioning over time.

bias_signals.detail: The brief frames the entire decision as 'whether to raise our entry plan from £59 to £79' with no mention of downstream effects on customer lifetime, competitive dynamics, or product tier mix — the model inherits that narrow scope.

The brief states the current price as £59 and the target as £79, and the mid-step option lands at £69 — all options are anchored symmetrically around the existing price point rather than derived from value or willingness-to-pay analysis.

The brief states 'Churn is currently 3% monthly' as a fixed fact with no range or uncertainty expressed, which may lead the model to treat baseline churn as more stable than it is when a price shock is applied.

elements_considered_but_excluded: Support cost change — no support-load factor exists in the current structure so adding it would require new elements beyond the brief
Brand perception — no brand or NPS factor is present; adding one would go beyond the stated scope

strengthen_items.label: Anchor the churn uplift to a price-elasticity assumption
strengthen_items.detail: The current baseline churn of 3% monthly is stated, but the model needs an explicit assumption about how much that rate rises per unit of price increase so that the Price-Driven Churn Uplift factor is bounded rather than open-ended.

strengthen_items.label: Add customer lifetime value as a second goal dimension
strengthen_items.detail: Focusing solely on Monthly Recurring Revenue can mask a scenario where higher price raises short-term revenue but accelerates attrition enough to destroy long-run value; a lifetime-value lens would surface that tension.

strengthen_items.label: Introduce a competitive response risk
strengthen_items.detail: A price rise may prompt prospects to evaluate alternatives more seriously, yet no risk capturing competitor attractiveness or switching behaviour currently feeds into the New Customer Conversion Drag or Active Customer Base factors.

strengthen_items.label: Constrain the grandfathering option with its revenue-delay cost
strengthen_items.detail: The Raise to £79 with Grandfathering option reduces churn risk but also delays full revenue uplift for existing customers; that trade-off should be made explicit as a constraint so it is weighed against the straight raise.
